source.title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables

accepted.question_text: For regular functions of several quaternionic variables, can one prove an analogue of the one-variable Taylor expansion theorem? Here H denotes the quaternion algebra; a regular function of n quaternionic variables is a differentiable function f: H^n -> H satisfying the left Cauchy-Fueter equation d f / d bar(q_i) = 0 in every variable. The one-variable theory uses homogeneous regular polynomials P_nu and the Cauchy-Kowalewski (C-K) product, which multiplies entire regular functions while staying regular; no analogous C-K product is known in several variables, and this absence blocks a Taylor series theory.
accepted.context_brief: Taylor expansions in several quaternionic variables

evidence.quote: An analogous C-K product is not known in the case of several variables; this fact prevents us from defining a Taylor series for regular functions defined on H^n.
We would like to point out that it is not known if it is possible to prove an analogous theorem to the case of regular functions of several quaternionic variables.

accepted.question_text: Give an analytic interpretation, valid for every n >= 2, of the matrix P_2 of first syzygies in the free resolution of the n-dimensional Cauchy-Fueter module M_n. The matrix P_2 encodes compatibility conditions for the non-homogeneous Cauchy-Fueter system d f / d bar(q_i) = g_i; for n = 2 these conditions have a simple quaternionic form, but for n = 3 the known 12 by 40 matrix gives ten quaternionic second-order compatibility conditions that the source says are not yet analytically understood.

evidence.quote: Problem: Give an analytic interpretation for the matrix P_2 of the first syzygies, for any n >= 2.
The matrix P_2 which appears in Theorem 3.2 is particularly important because it allows us to write explicitly the compatibility conditions for the non-homogeneous system.

accepted.question_text: In the free resolution of the Cauchy-Fueter module M_n from Theorem 3.2, prove or refute that every matrix in the resolution except P_2 has entries that are degree-one polynomials. The problem also asks for the analytic meaning of this observed linearity, since the authors report seeing it in computed examples but not knowing how to prove it in general.

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove that all the matrices which appear in Theorem 3.2 have entries which are degree one polynomials, with the exception of P_2.
However we have been unable to prove this fact in general, nor do we understand its analytical meaning.

accepted.question_text: Establish the relationship between the sheaf R of Cauchy-Fueter regular functions and the sheaf B^Q of hyperfunction solutions to the operator or matrix Q arising from the syzygy complex. For n = 2, the matrices P and Q originate the sheaves of regular and anti-regular functions respectively; for n = 3 and higher, Q is no longer simple, although P and Q have the same characteristic variety.

evidence.quote: Problem: Establish a relationship between R and B^Q.
For n=3 the matrix Q is not so simple anymore, and in general we do not know the relationship between the sheaves R and B^Q.

accepted.question_text: Find a (2n+1)-dimensional variety S inside H^n = R^(4n) for which the local cohomology of the sheaf R of Cauchy-Fueter regular functions with support in S vanishes in every degree j different from 2n-1 and is nonzero in degree 2n-1. This is intended as a quaternionic analogue of the classical pure n-codimensionality theorem for R^n inside C^n with respect to the sheaf O of holomorphic functions.

evidence.quote: Problem: Find a (2n+1)-dimensional variety S in H^n=R^(4n) such that H_S^j(H^n,R)=0 for all j not equal to 2n-1.
we need to prove a quaternionic analog of the classical theorem on the pure n-codimensionality of R^n in C^n, with respect to O.

accepted.question_text: When n = 2, can Theorem 3.8 on removability of compact singularities for regular functions be extended to include all 5-dimensional real subspaces of H^2? The stated theorem already gives removability for compact singularities contained in subspaces of dimensions 6, 7, and 8; dimension 4 is impossible, and dimension 5 is the unresolved borderline case not settled by the purely algebraic Ext-module method.

evidence.quote: Problem: Can Theorem 3.8 be extended, when n=2, to include all subspaces of dimension 5?
The case of dimension 5 cannot be solved by purely algebraic methods.

accepted.question_text: For the Cauchy-Fueter system P(D)f = 0, give a geometric characterization of the open sets that are P-convex. In the source, P-convexity is the weaker hypothesis that replaces ordinary convexity in the Ehrenpreis-Palamodov exactness theorem for systems of linear constant-coefficient differential operators, and it should express an appropriate relation between the system P and the topology of the open set.

evidence.quote: Problem: Give a geometric characterization of the P-convex sets.
when Omega is not convex the theorem still holds under the weaker hypothesis of P-convexity.

accepted.question_text: Construct a quaternionic Weyl algebra H[x, partial] with suitable variables x and differential operators partial. The construction must handle noncommutativity both in quaternionic coefficients and in variables, and it should be usable for systems of differential equations in the sense that the spaces R(U) of regular functions and F(U) of quaternionic hyperfunctions can be treated as modules over an algebra A_1(H).

evidence.quote: Problem: Construct a quaternionic Weyl algebra.
we have, apparently, a double non commutativity in both the coefficients and the variables.

accepted.question_text: Prove a Paley-Wiener theorem for the Fourier transform of compactly supported H-hyperfunctions, where H denotes the quaternion algebra and H-hyperfunctions are built from boundary values of quaternionic regular functions. The relevant Fourier transform should use the regular quaternionic exponential defined through the homogeneous regular polynomials P_nu, and the theorem should identify compact support with an appropriate space of entire functions of exponential type.

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove a Paley-Wiener Theorem for the Fourier transform of H-hyperfunctions.
The Fourier transform of a H-hyperfunction seems to be a quite complicated object, and the Paley-Wiener theorem ... has not been proved.

accepted.question_text: In quaternionic quantum mechanics, prove or disprove that the elements of the quaternionic scattering matrix are boundary values of regular quaternionic functions, in the sense of the quaternionic hyperfunctions introduced by the authors. The obstruction is that physicists use a formal analogue of exp(z) to build scattering matrices, but that exponential is not regular in the Cauchy-Fueter sense.
accepted.context_brief: Quaternionic scattering matrices as boundary values

evidence.quote: Problem: It is possible to prove that the elements of the quaternionic scattering matrix are boundary values of regular functions?
the non-regularity of the exponential function used in this case is an obstruction to restore the theory.

accepted.question_text: Apply the same algebraic analysis used for the Cauchy-Fueter system to the Moisil-Theodoresco system, the three-dimensional analogue and historical precursor of the Cauchy-Fueter system whose kernel has intrinsic physical interest and whose functions have natural regular extensions to H.
accepted.context_brief: Algebraic analysis of the Moisil-Theodoresco system

evidence.quote: Problem: Apply our algebraic analysis to the Moisil-Theodoresco system.
the so-called Moisil-Theodoresco system which is the 3-dimensional analogue ... of the Cauchy-Fueter system.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether results obtained from applying algebraic analysis to the Moisil-Theodoresco system can be used to obtain information about the Cauchy-Fueter system.

evidence.quote: Problem: Is it possible to use these results to get information on the Cauchy-Fueter system?

accepted.question_text: Given a hypercomplex algebra, study all possible families of operators that linearize the wave operator. This problem sits in the setting of hypercomplex operators that linearize ultrahyperbolic or wave-type operators, including operators related to Maxwell's system for biquaternion-valued functions and operators linearizing the Klein-Gordon equation using octonions.

evidence.quote: Problem: Given a hypercomplex algebra study all the possible families of operators linearizing the wave operator.
the authors ... have started to study some hypercomplex operators that are the linearization of some ultra-hyperbolic operators.

accepted.question_text: For the hypercomplex operators that linearize wave operators, study their fundamental solutions and provide integral formulas for the functions in their kernels.
accepted.context_brief: Fundamental solutions for hypercomplex wave linearizations

evidence.quote: Problem: Study the fundamental solution of such operators and provide integral formulas for the functions in their kernel.

accepted.question_text: Given a hypercomplex algebra A and a notion of A-regularity, find a hypercomplex algebra C and a corresponding notion of C-regularity such that every A-regular function of several variables appears as a special case of a C-regular function of one variable. The motivating examples are that regular functions of two quaternionic variables can be viewed as regular functions of one biquaternionic variable or one suitable Clifford variable.
accepted.context_brief: Several variables as one hypercomplex variable

evidence.quote: Problem: Given an hypercomplex algebra A and the notion of A-regularity, find a hypercomplex algebra C and a corresponding notion of C-regularity.
regular functions in two quaternionic variables can be seen as regular functions of one biquaternionic variable.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of regular functions of several octonion variables; compute the flabby dimension of the resulting sheaf of octonionic regular functions; and construct an analogue of the Moisil-Theodoresco operator in that octonionic setting. The source frames this as a continuation of earlier work on octonionic regular functions and the Cauchy-Fueter-Cayley operator.

evidence.quote: Problem: Develop such a theory, compute the flabby dimension of the sheaf of octonionic regular functions, and construct an analogue of the Moisil-Theodoresco operator.
it may be interesting to utilize our approach to develop a theory of regular functions of several octonion variables.

Mapped the PDF. Major sections: 1 Introduction; 2 Regular functions of a quaternionic variable; 3 The Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables; 4 Open problems; References. Definitions include the quaternion algebra H, left and right Cauchy-Fueter operators, regular functions, the C-K product, the sheaf R of regular functions, the Cauchy-Fueter module M_n, syzygy matrices P and P_2, B^Q, and H-hyperfunctions. Open-problem regions occur in page 6 and pages 12-18.
Extracted an implicit open question from Section 2, where the source says an analogue of the one-variable Taylor theorem is not known for regular functions of several quaternionic variables.
